stem: Organic compounds can be distinguished using chemical tests and analytical techniques.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Complete Table 3.1 to:
- identify a reagent which can distinguish between the compounds in each pair
- give the **positive** result of the chemical test **and** identify which compound shows this result.

Use a different reagent for each test.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
$\mathbf{A1}$ and $\mathbf{A2}$ are structural isomers.

Define structural isomers.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Identify the type of polymer that forms from $\mathbf{D2}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Draw one repeat unit of polymer $\mathbf{Z}$.

Fig. 3.1 shows the infrared spectrum of $\mathbf{E}$. parts.text:
Use the two infrared spectra and Table 3.2 to identify the functional group present only in $\mathbf{E}$.
Explain your answer, referring only to absorptions at frequencies greater than $1500\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the infrared spectrum of $\mathbf{F}$ to identify the functional group formed when $\mathbf{E}$ reacts with cold dilute acidified $\text{KMnO}_4\text{(aq)}$.
Explain your answer, referring only to absorptions at frequencies greater than $1500\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The mass spectrum of $\mathbf{E}$ shows a molecular ion peak and an M+2 peak of approximately equal abundance at $m/e = 120$ and 122.

Deduce the relative molecular mass, $M_{\text{r}}$, of $\mathbf{E}$.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Use the information in 3(c) to suggest a structure for $\mathbf{E}$.

parts.label: (c)(v)
parts.text:
Complete the equation for the reaction of $\mathbf{E}$ with cold dilute acidified $\text{KMnO}_4\text{(aq)}$ to form $\mathbf{F}$. In the equation, $[\text{O}]$ represents cold dilute acidified $\text{KMnO}_4\text{(aq)}$.
$$\text{H}_2\text{O} + [\text{O}] + \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
$\mathbf{C2}$ can be synthesised using $\mathbf{A1}$ as a single organic reactant.

{{figure:pdf_visual_04.png}}
parts.text:
Devise a multi-step synthetic route to form $\mathbf{C2}$ from $\mathbf{A1}$.
Identify relevant reagents and conditions, and state the organic products of each step.
